description.value: The study examined whether Network Centrality in the frontotemporoinsular network is disrupted in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia and whether it is associated with social-executive performance, comparing bvFTD patients with healthy controls and frontoinsular stroke patients.

spans.text: We examine (i) whether Network Centrality (a graph theory metric that measures how important a node is in a brain network) in the frontotemporoinsular network is disrupted in bvFTD, and (ii) the level of involvement of this network in social-executive performance.

value: We hypothesized that the NC of the frontotemporoinsular network would discriminate bvFTD patients from controls, and from stroke patients, and that it would be associated with social-executive performance.

value: Compared with frontoinsular stroke patients, bvFTD patients showed significantly decreased Network Centrality in the bilateral and right frontotemporoinsular network; this suggests that the centrality alteration is specific to bvFTD neurodegeneration rather than a broad neurological condition.

spans.text: Thus, our results suggest that the centrality alterations of the frontotemporoinsular network are a distinctive connectivity hallmark of neurodegeneration in bvFTD.
